subject: Setup for analyzing fractionated label-free data

messages.author: ab4c9ed2cd29563b
messages.subject: Setup for analyzing fractionated label-free data
parts:
Hello,
I have been handed a set of in-gel digest data which we'd like to analyze via label-free quantification. Extracting intensities to use as input into MSstats is relatively straightforward, but my question is with regard to the input data matrix.
As I understand it, MSstats requires a line in the input data for every feature in every LC-MS/MS run. However for in-gel data we _expect_ most peptides to _not_ show up in a given run, due to the fractionation.

Is it more appropriate to input an extremely sparse data matrix to MSstats with NA for every run in which a peptide wasn't seen, or should the intensities be merged across runs beforehand in this case?

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: Setup for analyzing fractionated label-free data
parts:
Dear Jason,

in your case, it is not necessary to have a row for every feature per run. Since each fraction (in principle) contains separate peptide or protein species, you only need to add rows with NA for the corresponding fraction. For example, if peptide1 appears in fraction3, you should have a row for each peptide in fraction3 of every sample (and NA for fraction3 of the samples where the peptide was not observed). You do not need to add rows in the other fractions. 

An analogy is in targeted proteomics, where experiments may have more peptide targets than what can be acquired in a single run. Then the targets are split into multiple 'methods', and the peptide only needs all the rows in its own 'method'. The 'methods' can be thought of an an analogy for fractions. See section 2.1.1(i) of the user manual for more details.

HTH
Olga
